content.title: Computers are very literal
content.body: Computers do exactly what you tell them — nothing more, nothing less. If you say "spread peanut butter" but forget to say "open the jar first," a computer would try to spread from a closed jar. It won't guess what you meant. Ever.

content.title: Order matters — a lot
content.body: Computers follow instructions in the exact order you give them. Step 1 always happens before Step 2. If you put instructions in the wrong order, you'll get a different result — or an error. There are no shortcuts.

content.title: The sandwich test
content.body: Imagine telling a robot to make you a sandwich. Your instructions say: "1. Spread peanut butter. 2. Open the jar." The robot will try to spread from a closed jar — and fail. Computers need every step spelled out, in the right order, with nothing left to imagination.

content.title: This is why bugs happen
content.body: Most beginner mistakes in coding come from a missing step, a wrong order, or a tiny spelling error. It's not a sign you're bad at coding — it's just how precise computers need to be. Once you understand this, bugs feel less mysterious and much easier to fix.

quiz.question: If your instructions are unclear, a computer will try to guess what you meant.
quiz.explanation: False! Computers follow instructions literally and exactly. They don't guess, infer, or fill in the blanks — that's what makes precision so important.

quiz.question: Your robot sandwich instructions say: "1. Pour the milk. 2. Open the milk carton." What happens?

options.text: The robot pours the milk perfectly
The robot opens the carton first because it's smarter than that
The robot tries to pour from a closed carton
The robot asks you what to do

quiz.explanation: The robot follows instructions in order — Step 1 is "pour the milk," so it tries, even though the carton is closed. Computers don't reorder steps on their own.

quiz.question: What is the most common cause of bugs (mistakes) in code?

options.text: A missing step, wrong order, or spelling error in the instructions

quiz.explanation: Almost all beginner bugs come down to a missing step, instructions in the wrong order, or a tiny typo. Knowing this makes debugging much less frustrating.

quiz.question: The order you write instructions in doesn't affect what a program does.
quiz.explanation: False! Order is everything. Computers execute instructions top to bottom, in sequence. Swap two steps and you get a completely different (often broken) result.
